I had the same reaction as Gaffney. The "guess the historical person from context" parlour game is exactly what I had hoped contest entries would avoid, and this goes one worse by making it "guess the Foundation reference".

That said, there are some nifty touches here (the summoning of pistols was particularly neat), and I could see myself upvoting works in this canon. But I'd encourage a slightly more gonzo approach to the material - more "Wild Wild West" than what's currently there.

item.content:encoded:
It's funny, but I actually dislike this tale for the exact reasons that you like it. Maybe it's an artifact of living in the real "West" (namely, Arizona) but I don't particularly enjoy romanticization of it. After a while, spaghetti westerns become old hat, and the fact that their idealized and inaccurate depiction of the West is often times the only thing people associate with the area irl is rather tiresome.

Instead of yet another hackneyed, cliched, glorified version of the western frontier, it would be nice to see a more realistic, down-to-earth depiction. Sadly, this is not it.

It's a well written tale, but it's not to my taste.

item.content:encoded:
The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly theme music plays.

I found this tale to be entertaining on two fronts. As a romanticization of the Wild West I feel you do a good job capturing that spaghetti western feel in how your cast of interact with each other. As an SCP tale, the subtle and no-so-subtle references to characters, skips, GoIs, and the like are highly amusing and do give the tale that SCP flavor needed to tie into the site.

+1.

item.content:encoded:
Special thanks to Roget, Dexanote, and many others for their help in refining this. I was weighing posting this as a history contest entry or not, and decided on making it an entry. This is supposed to be a starter tale for a Old West Canon myself and Dexanote and a few others are working on right now.

Spoilers below:

+ show block
– hide block

This tale includes old west versions of Dr. Wondertainment, A Little Mister, Anderson, SCP-076, SCP-073, SCP-106, SCP-049, SCP-682 and Dr. Kondraki. I think I might be missing one or two references actually but I'll check back later.

Title of the tale is a reference to a poem by Housman, which you'll find in its entirety here:

Now hollow fires burn out to black,
And lights are guttering low:
Square your shoulders, lift your pack,
And leave your friends and go.

Oh never fear, man, nought’s to dread,
Look not left nor right:
In all the endless road you tread
There’s nothing but the night.
A. E. Housman
